In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the film 'Cane Arise' is a film that has a lot to offer in the way of the Caribbean culture, its people and its history, as well as the history of the African Diaspora.
the Caribbean is a cultural mosaic, and that the Caribbean people have been influenced by the cultures of their ancestors, and by the cultures of the people who have settled in the Caribbean.
the Caribbean is a place where the black people of the world have been thrown together, and where, in the context of the post colonial, they have had to struggle for a sense of their own identity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have attempted to show how the Caribbean is an important site for the study of diaspora, cultural hybridity and cultural identity.
we have been trying to understand the relationship between culture and identity, the ways in which they are being represented and the ways in which we can represent ourselves.

the cultural identity of a people is not only a product of the past but also of their present and future, and that it can be changed by the people themselves, by their own will and by their own actions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we are all, to a greater or lesser extent, 'hybrid','mestizos', 'creolized' and 'diasporic' subjects.
the Caribbean is a place where the black subject is not only at the centre of the representation, but is the subject of the representation.
cultural identity is not an 'already accomplished fact' or a 'fixed destiny' but rather, it is something which is always 'in process' and always constituted within representation.
